title.zh: 分子氢四族碰撞矩阵组装

summary: Assemble the charge-exchange, two momentum-transfer and self-collision stress matrices on a cylindrical normalized velocity grid. The H/D laboratory-energy scaling is explicit; elastic matrices retain their sign, and the angular node count can be increased for an explicit convergence check. The complete result is returned as one scirel._result.Result mapping; mapping access is retained and non-colliding fields also support attribute access.

capability: Assemble charge-exchange, two momentum-transfer and self-collision stress matrices on a cylindrical normalized velocity grid.
operation: Assemble the four-family molecular-hydrogen collision matrices
normalized cylindrical velocity axes, cell weights, normalization energy and mass ratio -> four SIG matrices and accompanying geometry
discovery.model: Axisymmetric velocity-space integration kernels; momentum-transfer and viscosity cross sections use different isotope scalings.
discovery.geometry: Cylindrical velocity space with a uniform midpoint azimuthal average (five points by default, n_theta explicitly increaseable); vr and vx are dimensionless v/Vth and source/target pairs flatten in Fortran order.
discovery.boundary: vr positive and strictly increasing, vx strictly increasing, radial weights nonnegative, axial weights positive, Tnorm and mu positive and finite; vx need not cross zero; n_theta must be a positive integer; elastic matrices retain their sign.

identity.relation: molecular H2 four-family normalized collision-kernel matrix assembly
identity.direction: normalized cylindrical velocity axes, cell weights, normalization energy and mass ratio -> four SIG matrices and the accompanying geometry
identity.definition: Let g^2 = vr_i^2 + vr_k^2 - 2*vr_i*vr_k*cos(theta) + (vx_j - vx_l)^2 and theta_m = pi*(m + 1/2)/n_theta. Matrix column weights are Vr2pidVr_k*dVx_l, with Fortran ordering row = i + nvr*j and col = k + nvr*l. The CX kernel is <g*sigma_CX>, the mixed momentum kernel is (vx_j - vx_l)*<g*sigma_mt>, and the self-collision stress kernel is <(g_perp^2 - 2*g_x^2)*g*sigma_vis>*3/8. Vth^2 = 2*Q*Tnorm/(mu*H_MASS). The molecular CX fit energy is g^2*2*Tnorm/mu, H2-H and H2-P are g^2*Tnorm/mu, and the self viscosity is g^2*2*Tnorm.
identity.model: axisymmetric velocity-space integration kernels; momentum-transfer and viscosity cross sections use different isotope scalings
identity.geometry: cylindrical velocity space with a uniform midpoint azimuthal average, five points by default; n_theta can be increased explicitly
identity.coordinates: vr and vx are dimensionless v/Vth; source and target velocity pairs flatten in Fortran order
identity.boundary: positive and strictly increasing vr, strictly increasing vx, nonnegative radial weights, positive axial weights, and positive finite Tnorm and mu; vx is not required to cross zero. n_theta must be a positive integer; the outputs retain negative values of the elastic kernels
assumptions: Constants H_MASS = 1.6726231e-27 kg and Q = 1.602177e-19 C; Vth = sqrt(2*Q*Tnorm/(mu*H_MASS)), and every node uses v/Vth.

The fit argument is the laboratory energy of the relevant projectile in the stationary-target frame, not always a center-of-mass energy. Momentum transfer maps E_D to E_D/2 for the hydrogen fits and viscosity maps E_D to E_D; H (mu=1) and D (mu=2) are verified, and other positive mu values are only an algebraic extension without new physical qualification.

The molecular CX projectile mass is 2*H_MASS; the mixed H-H2/P-H2 fits always use the H projectile mass, and exchanging the test particle and the background does not change the relative-speed cross section.
Molecular self viscosity uses the momentum-transfer fit as an approximate surrogate; no independent molecular-viscosity measurement is bound.
The default five-angle rule is a numerical approximation; the caller must independently check angular and velocity-grid convergence.

inputs.name: vr
inputs.constraints: nonempty, finite, positive and strictly increasing

inputs.name: vx
inputs.constraints: nonempty, finite and strictly increasing; may be shifted as a whole and is not required to cross zero

inputs.name: Vr2pidVr
inputs.constraints: finite and nonnegative, aligned with vr

inputs.name: dVx
inputs.constraints: finite and positive, aligned with vx

inputs.name: Tnorm
inputs.description: normalization energy that defines the thermal speed
inputs.constraints: finite positive real scalar; arrays, booleans and strings are rejected

inputs.name: mu
inputs.description: isotope mass ratio: 1 for hydrogen and 2 for deuterium
inputs.constraints: finite positive real scalar; physical checks are limited to H=1 and D=2

inputs.name: n_theta
inputs.description: number of azimuthal midpoint nodes; used for an explicit convergence check
inputs.constraints: positive integer; booleans are rejected. Default 5

outputs.name: SIG_H2_H
outputs.constraints: finite; positive, negative and zero values are retained

outputs.name: SIG_H2_P
outputs.constraints: finite; positive, negative and zero values are retained

outputs.name: SIG_H2_H2
outputs.description: signed self-collision stress kernel, including the viscosity cross section and the 3/8 factor
outputs.constraints: finite; positive, negative and zero values are retained

outputs.name: v_v2
outputs.description: normalized squared relative speed at each angular node

outputs.name: vr2_vx2
outputs.description: relative radial squared term minus twice the axial squared term
outputs.constraints: finite; positive, negative and zero values are retained

outputs.name: vx_vx
outputs.constraints: finite; positive, negative and zero values are retained

outputs.name: Vth2
outputs.description: square of the thermal speed scale

preconditions: each channel uses the declared laboratory energy, isotope scaling, cross-section fit and endpoint clipping
the caller checks finite angular and velocity integration accuracy for the intended use; arrays are flattened in Fortran order
supported: H/D four-channel matrix assembly, a common axial velocity shift, and weighted exchange symmetry or antisymmetry
excluded: full transport-equation solution, cross-call cache lifetime, other species, and unverified isotope extrapolation
inferring accuracy for arbitrary distributions or new experimental cross-section qualification from a finite node count

failure_semantics.invalid_input: raises ValueError for non-real or non-finite values, mismatched shapes, non-increasing axes, invalid weights or normalization, or an invalid n_theta
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: raises ValueError when the thermal speed, a cross section or a matrix is not representable as a finite value; an out-of-memory failure also returns no partial matrix
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: a finite midpoint quadrature with no adaptive iteration; convergence is the caller's check
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial scirel._result.Result mapping is returned on error.

python.signature: assemble_molecular_hydrogen_collision_matrices(vr, vx, Vr2pidVr, dVx, Tnorm, mu=1.0, *, n_theta=5)

example.description: build a two-by-two velocity grid and check the signed matrices and the default five-angle geometry
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel._result import Result
from scirel.collisions import assemble_molecular_hydrogen_collision_matrices
r = assemble_molecular_hydrogen_collision_matrices(
    vr=np.array([0.5, 1.0]), vx=np.array([-1.0, 1.0]),
    Vr2pidVr=np.array([1.0, 2.0]), dVx=np.array([2.0, 2.0]), Tnorm=1.0,
)
assert isinstance(r, Result)
assert r.SIG_CX is r['SIG_CX']
assert r['SIG_CX'].shape == (4, 4)
assert r['v_v2'].shape == (2, 2, 2, 2, 5)
assert np.isfinite(r['SIG_H2_H2']).all()
assert (r['SIG_H2_H2'] < 0).any()
assert r['Vth2'].shape == (1,)
example.expected: four finite 4x4 matrices; CX is nonnegative and the elastic moments retain negative values; the five-angle geometry and the thermal-speed square are returned The top-level result is a scirel._result.Result mapping while all ten fields remain the same arrays.

scope: independent geometry and fit comparisons retain the existing numerical tolerances
H/D four-channel 4096-angle midpoint results are compared with independent SciPy adaptive integration; weighted exchange relations and a common boost are checked
moments and Alpha from real normalized distributions verify H<->H2 momentum exchange, Maxwell equilibrium momentum and weak drift
Top-level Result type and attribute/key equivalence are regression-tested; nested array fields remain plain NumPy arrays.
verification.evidence_ceiling: supports consistency of the declared velocity integration kernels with the tested discrete inputs; it is not experimental cross-section validation over all energy ranges and does not constitute full physical qualification
known_limitations: fit endpoint clipping and the molecular viscosity surrogate are model approximations
the default five-angle rule has no universal accuracy guarantee; higher-order checks do not replace the caller's grid convergence
human scientific acceptance and redistribution licensing are decided separately; the verification gap is not closed by this file

The self-collision prefactor is the Boltzmann value 3/8, which reproduces the Chapman-Enskog hard-sphere p/mu. The KN1D report (LaBombard, PSFC/RR-01-3, Appendix B) has 1/8 because it equates the BGK integral of (2 v_x^2 - v_r^2), three times that of v_x^2, to the v_x^2 rate; results here therefore differ from KN1D by that factor in this channel.
